Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Record Class MetalThemeSpec

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.MetalThemeSpec
public record MetalThemeSpec(String name, Color primary1, Color primary2, Color primary3, Color secondary1, Color secondary2, Color secondary3) extends Record
An immutable, persistence-friendly description of a Swing Metal theme: a display name plus the six MetalTheme palette colours (three "primary" shades used for selection/focus chrome and three "secondary" shades used for the control backgrounds).

This is the pure seam of the 2D desktop's Metal theme manager. Everything here - the built-in palettes, the compact encode/decode serialisation used to persist user-created themes, and the accent-colour derivation behind "New theme" - is display-independent and unit-tested headless. Turning a spec into a live MetalTheme and pushing it through MetalLookAndFeel is CustomMetalTheme's and MetalThemeManager's job.

The encoded form is name;#rrggbb;#rrggbb;#rrggbb;#rrggbb;#rrggbb; #rrggbb (seven ';'-separated fields); a list of themes encodes one spec per line. A malformed record decodes to null and is skipped, so a corrupt preference can never take the desktop down.

    • GLASSY

      public static final MetalThemeSpec GLASSY
      "Glassy" - reproduces, as faithfully as a six-colour Metal palette allows, the translucent ice-blue "glass" look of the native 3D desktop's Frame3D window chrome. Every shade below is lifted directly from the 3D rendering code rather than picked freehand, so the 2D desktop reads as the same material:
      • primary1/primary2 are the exact edge/title accent blues org.jdesktop.lg3d.widgets.builtin.WidgetPanel's BORDER (0x6094D6) and TITLE_COLOR (0x8CB9F5) paint on every glassy HUD card and window decoration;
      • primary3 is org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.shape. FrostedGlassPanel's DEFAULT_TINT - the cool, lightly-blue frosted-white tint (RGB 0.85, 0.90, 1.00) every Frame3D glass panel is washed with - rounded to 0xD9E6FF;
      • the secondary ramp is a neutral extension of that same tint (a muted slate-blue shadow down to a near-white glass background) so controls and panels stay legible while keeping the icy, translucent character.

  • Method Details

    • fromAccent

      public static MetalThemeSpec fromAccent(String name, Color accent)
      Derives a full theme from a single accent colour: the accent becomes primary2, a darkened shade becomes primary1 and a lightened shade primary3, while the neutral secondary ramp is borrowed from Steel. This backs the control center's "New theme" action, so a user picks one colour rather than six.
